title: Perf Canary Dashboards — Mockups + Drilldown Flows (v0)
content:
Slide 1 — Title / context
Perf Canary Dashboards — Mockups + Drilldown Flows (v0)
Owner: Felix (Observability Pack)
Reviewers: Allison/Logan/Nadia/SRE
Date: 2026-01-10 (updated through 2026-01-28)

Notes:
- This deck is meant to unblock ENG-2847 (dashboards) by agreeing on navigation + minimum viable panels.
- Mockups are intentionally rough; we’ll implement in Grafana once label schema + annotations are final.


Slide 2 — What we’re trying to answer (operator questions)
Primary questions an oncall asks when a perf regression alert fires:
1) Is the signal real (enough samples / not deploy window / not warmup artifacts)?
2) What changed? (runtime build, scheduler mode, kernel selection, GPU SKU, region)
3) How bad is it? (p95 latency delta vs baseline; tokens/sec delta vs baseline)
4) Is it isolated? (one model family? one region? one GPU SKU?)
5) What’s the fastest mitigation? (rollback runtime, pin scheduler mode, disable heuristic X, route away from SKU)

Notes:
- The dashboards should be usable even without reading the design doc.
- “Time to first triage hypothesis” is the KPI here, not pretty charts.


Slide 3 — Dashboard inventory (proposed)
A) Overview: Perf Canary — Fleet Health (landing)
B) Model/Region: Perf Canary — Model Detail
C) Slice Explorer: Perf Canary — Slice Compare (GPU/runtime/scheduler)
D) Debug: Perf Canary — Kernel + Scheduler Attribution
E) Alert Context: Perf Canary — Recent Alerts (table-ish) + links

Notes:
- “Overview” must load quickly and have low cardinality queries.
- “Debug” can be heavier; likely only used by Runtime engineers.


Slide 4 — Navigation + drilldown flow (happy path)
Flow when paged:
1) Open alert → links to Model Detail with params pre-filled
2) Model Detail → click “Suspect slice” (region/gpu/runtime) → Slice Compare
3) Slice Compare → click runtime_build → “Deploy diff” link + “Kernel attribution” dashboard
4) Kernel attribution → identify kernel_id/fallback_reason shift OR scheduler queue behavior shift
5) If mitigation needed → follow runbook link + rollback decision

Notes:
- Make links deterministic: all dashboards share template variable names.
- Alert payload should include direct links (with model/region/gpu/runtime_build already selected).


Slide 5 — Template variables (agreement needed)
Global variables (consistent across dashboards):
- region (enum; default = all)
- model (enum; default = all)
- gpu_sku (enum; default = all)
- runtime_build (enum; default = latest)
- scheduler_mode (enum; default = all)
- traffic_class (fixed to canary-safe / source=perf-canary)
- stream (bool; streaming vs non-streaming)
- prompt_shape (small set; see workload matrix)

Notes:
- Keep variables minimal. If we can’t support a variable without exploding cardinality, we should remove it.
- “runtime_build=latest” is not the same as “baseline”; baseline is a comparison series.


Slide 6 — Overview dashboard mockup (Perf Canary — Fleet Health)
Wireframe:
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Header: Perf Canary — Fleet Health                                               |
| Filters: [time range] [region=*] [model=*] [gpu_sku=*] [stream=*]                |
| Links: Runbook | Metric Spec | Canary Status Page | Recent Deploys               |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 1: KPI tiles (last 30m / 6h)                                                 |
| [# models regressing p95] [# models regressing tps] [canary req rate] [errors]   |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 2: Heatmap (Model x Region)                                                  |
| - Color = p95 latency regression % vs baseline                                   |
| - Toggle = tokens/sec regression % vs baseline                                   |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 3: Top regressions table (clickable)                                         |
| Columns: model | region | gpu_sku | p95_delta% | tps_delta% | samples | build     |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Notes:
- Heatmap is the fastest way to see scope/blast radius.
- “Top regressions” table should match alert grouping keys (dedup).
- MVP can omit “gpu_sku” in heatmap; keep heatmap at model/region, then drill down.

Open question:
- Do we want separate heatmaps for streaming vs non-streaming, or a single toggle? (I lean toggle.)


Slide 7 — Model Detail dashboard mockup (Perf Canary — Model Detail)
Wireframe:
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Header: Model Detail                                                             |
| Filters: [model=LLama-?] [region=us-east] [gpu_sku=*] [stream=*] [prompt_shape=*]|
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 1: Time series (p95 latency)                                                 |
| - Series A: observed p95 (canary)                                                |
| - Series B: baseline p95 (rolling 7d median OR pinned known-good)                |
| - Shaded: deploy window suppression periods                                      |
| - Annotations: runtime deploy events (git sha / version)                         |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 2: Time series (tokens/sec)                                                  |
| - Observed vs baseline                                                           |
| - Note: show both request-level TPS and decode-only TPS? (TBD)                   |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 3: “At a glance” slice cards                                                 |
| [Worst GPU SKU] [Worst runtime_build] [Worst scheduler_mode] [Worst prompt_shape]|
| Each card shows delta% + samples + deep link                                     |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 4: Supporting signals (small panels)                                         |
| - error_rate                                                                     |
| - time_to_first_token p95 (streaming only)                                       |
| - batch_size distribution / continuous batching stats                            |
| - kv_cache_hit_rate (if available in canary tag)                                 |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Notes:
- Model Detail is where we expect 80% of triage to happen.
- Keep it readable: 2 big charts, then slice cards.

Open questions:
- Should baseline line be selectable (rolling vs pinned) in the UI, or pinned by alert type?
- Do we need “prefill_p95” and “decode_p95” split in v1, or is end-to-end p95 enough?


Slide 8 — Slice Compare mockup (Perf Canary — Slice Compare)
Goal: isolate “which slice is driving regression?”

Wireframe:
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Header: Slice Compare                                                            |
| Filters: [model] [region] [stream] [prompt_shape]                                |
| Compare by: (dropdown) gpu_sku | runtime_build | scheduler_mode                  |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 1: Bar chart (delta vs baseline)                                             |
| - Bars: each value of selected dimension (e.g., each GPU SKU)                    |
| - Metrics: p95_delta% and tps_delta% (toggle or dual axis)                       |
| - Only show if samples >= min_samples                                            |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 2: Time series small multiples                                               |
| - One mini chart per slice (top N worst)                                         |
| - Click slice → opens Model Detail with that slice pinned                        |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Notes:
- This dashboard is the bridge between SRE “is this wide?” and Runtime “which knob?”
- Must include sample counts and/or confidence guardrails (min samples).

Open question:
- How do we represent “unknown/other” values without silently hiding them? (E.g., gpu_sku missing label.)


Slide 9 — Kernel + Scheduler Attribution mockup (Perf Canary — Kernel/Scheduler)
Use case: “regression correlates with runtime build, now what inside runtime?”

Wireframe:
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Header: Kernel + Scheduler Attribution                                           |
| Filters: [model] [region] [gpu_sku] [runtime_build] [scheduler_mode]             |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 1: Kernel selection distribution                                             |
| - Pie or stacked area: selected_kernel_id share over time                        |
| - Table: kernel_id | share% | median latency | fallback_reason top               |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 2: Scheduler health                                                          |
| - queue_time_p95 (if available)                                                  |
| - active_batches / queued_requests                                               |
| - batch composition stats (prefill_count/decode_count, max_seq_len)              |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Row 3: “What changed?” annotation strip                                          |
| - runtime deploy events (git sha)                                                |
| - config pinning changes (if we can emit)                                        |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Notes:
- This is not required for initial phase-1 rollout, but we should ensure the drilldown exists.
- Kernel attribution MUST be gated behind canary tag to control overhead (per runtime plan).

Open questions:
- Do we have stable kernel_id semantics across versions? If kernel_id mapping changes, attribution might mislead.


Slide 10 — Deploy annotations + “diff” links (how we want it to feel)
Proposal:
- All key charts show vertical markers on runtime deploy.
- Clicking an annotation opens a “deploy info” panel (Grafana data link) with:
  - runtime_version
  - git_sha
  - deploy_id / build_id
  - rollout phase (if available)
  - link: “compare previous build” (GitHub compare URL or internal release diff)

Example data link format (draft):
- https://github.com/redwood/redwood/compare/${prev_sha}...${sha}
- internal: /console/deploys/${deploy_id}

Notes:
- This is the single most important UX feature besides “baseline vs observed”.

Open question:
- Where is the source of truth for prev_sha per region? (Release Eng doc suggests we can compute from deploy events.)


Slide 11 — Alert payload ↔ dashboard alignment
What should be in the alert (so dashboards open correctly):
- model
- region
- gpu_sku (if known)
- runtime_build (suspect)
- scheduler_mode (if pinned)
- stream
- prompt_shape
- p95_delta% + baseline method
- tps_delta% + baseline method
- sample count + time window
- links:
  - Model Detail (prefilled)
  - Slice Compare (prefilled compare=gpu_sku by default)
  - Runbook
  - “recent deploys” view

Notes:
- Rafael asked that alerts be actionable without needing to manually set 5 filters.
- Also: alert should include “suppression reason” if in deploy/maintenance window.

Open question:
- Do we want 2 alert types (p95 regression vs tokens/sec regression) or 1 combined? If 2, dashboards should show both anyway.


Slide 12 — Cardinality / performance constraints (implementation guardrails)
Constraints we’ve heard from Telemetry:
- We cannot ship dashboards that query high-cardinality label sets by default.
- Allowed core labels (tentative): model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, stream, prompt_shape.
- “kernel_id” and “fallback_reason” should only be queried when runtime_build and model are pinned (narrow scope).

Dashboard guardrails:
- Overview:
  - aggregate over gpu_sku by default
  - don’t show per-runtime_build series by default (maybe show only “current build vs baseline”)
- Model Detail:
  - show only 1-2 series + baseline
  - slice cards computed by pre-aggregated metrics if possible
- Slice Compare:
  - limit to top N slices (e.g., 10) by worst delta to avoid long legends

Notes:
- We should consider recording rules / pre-aggregations specifically for the dashboards.

Open question:
- Do we need separate recording rules per stream mode to avoid “toggle queries” being slow?


Slide 13 — Open questions (to resolve this week)
1) Baseline selector UX
- Should users switch rolling vs pinned in the dashboard, or should dashboards follow alert’s baseline choice?

2) tokens/sec definition for streaming
- What exactly are we plotting (request-level end-to-end TPS vs decode-only)?
- For streaming, do we annotate first-token alignment fix (PR 39157) as a “definition change” event?

3) Warmup/caching artifacts
- Do we need an explicit “warmup excluded” indicator on charts?
- Should Model Detail always show a “cache priming” signal so responders don’t chase false regressions?

4) Drilldown ownership boundaries
- SRE wants quick yes/no + mitigation.
- Runtime wants kernel attribution.
- Do we keep one dashboard with collapsible rows, or separate dashboards to keep things simple?

5) Region vs GPU slicing
- If a regression appears region-scoped but is actually a GPU SKU change within region, how do we surface that quickly?


Slide 14 — Next steps / asks
Immediate next steps:
- Felix: implement Overview + Model Detail in observability-pack (target PR by end of week)
- Nadia/Logan: confirm label schema + which metrics are safe for recording rules
- Sean/Rafael: confirm alert grouping keys and ensure “Top regressions table” matches them
- Noah/Sofia/Hiro: confirm which runtime signals are stable enough to include (queue_time, kernel_id, fallback_reason)

Asks / decisions needed:
- Approve the dashboard inventory (A–D) and the variable set.
- Confirm whether baseline toggle is needed in UI.

Appendix link placeholders (to be added when docs/URLs finalized):
- Runbook: Perf Canary Regression Triage
- Metric Spec: Perf Canary Metric Spec
- ADR: Baseline Strategy

Notes:
- If we can’t finalize baseline semantics this week, we can still ship Overview/Model Detail with observed metrics + deploy annotations, then add baseline overlay once detector logic is stable.
